learning_outcomes.text: Knows basic concepts, classification of power networks, network structure, network systems and their properties.
Knows the principles of modeling elements and complex network systems for steady-state calculations (power flows).
Student knows the construction of electrical devices used in the generation, transmission, distribution and use of electrical energy.
Student knows the threats to which electrical power devices and switchgears are exposed.

The student is able to calculate characteristic electrical quantities determining the selection of electrical power devices and apparatus under normal operating conditions and during fault conditions.
Is able to perform calculations of power flows, voltage drops and power losses in open networks.
Student is able to work in a group when performing laboratory exercises.

syllabus_topics: Testing of electric shock protection measures
Reactive power compensation
Testing of light sources and control systems
Testing the current carrying capacity of flexible and rigid conductors
Analysis of power flow in a high voltage network
Organizational information and topics of classes. Basic concepts and definitions. Requirements for networks. Classification of electrical power networks
Structure and components of overhead lines. Normative requirements. Low voltage and medium voltage insulated overhead lines
Network systems. Development of electrical power networks
Structure and components of cable lines. Construction and designation of cables. Laying methods. Special HV cables. Cable accessories
Analysis of operating conditions of distribution electrical power network - modeling and performing network calculations in steady state (power flows)
Analysis of medium voltage network operating conditions
Principles of electrical network calculations. Equivalent circuits of network elements. Determination of quadripole parameters and operations on quadripoles
Calculation of network status (current flows, voltage drops) in open and closed networks. Load estimation. Numerical network modeling - principles and methods
Criteria and principles for selecting conductor and cable cross-sections
Power and electrical energy losses in networks. Principles for calculating losses. Methods for limiting losses
Methods and ways of voltage regulation in networks. Reactive power compensation
Electrical devices in the electrical power system. Basic concepts
Exposures and operating conditions of electrical power devices. Supply reliability
General division and functions of electrical apparatus, switchgears and distribution boards
Division of switches and their basic parameters, constructions of circuit breakers and selection criteria at different voltage levels
Construction of disconnectors, switch-disconnectors, earthing switches, isolating switch-disconnectors and contactors. Selection principles
Current and voltage transformers. Electrical power stations. Electrical power switchgears
assessment_rules: Lectures are assessed by an examination. Laboratory classes are assessed based on the execution of the exercises, a test, and the completion of the classes. To pass the module, all laboratory classes must be completed. Students are required to prepare for laboratory exercises, which may be verified by an oral or written colloquium, and successful completion involves presenting a solution to the problem posed.
